examples.name: nth
examples.title: Refinement types, by example
examples.description: The page walkthrough: len and append prove inductively, and the bound 0 <= i < len l rides nth's parameter as a contract, turning the Nil arm into a false obligation rather than an exception.

examples.name: overview
examples.title: Sixty seconds
examples.description: First contact: a division whose divisor carries a not (_ = 0) contract, discharged at each call site. The smallest end-to-end proof.

examples.name: reflect
examples.title: The program as its own spec
examples.description: total_ recursive functions reflect into the logic, so len, mem and depth denote themselves in refinements -- no separate spec library, no proof text.

examples.name: tuples
examples.title: Native tuples in refinements
examples.description: Construction, fst/snd projection, tuple-pattern matching and structural equality, reasoned through Lean's product structures.

examples.name: quant
examples.title: Quantifiers in predicates
examples.description: forall_, exists_ and native implication in refinements, with notes on where grind's automation is reliable and where quantified reasoning belongs in a prelude block.

examples.name: fib
examples.title: Fibonacci: fast doubling, one file
examples.description: The naive recursion is reflected and total; the O(log n) fast-doubling loop is verified against it. The addition and doubling identities are proved by functional induction in an embedded [%%vox.lean] block -- put the cursor there and ask for the live Lean goal.

examples.name: reverse
examples.title: In-place array reverse (McCarthy stores)
examples.description: Mutable-array verification via McCarthy upd/elem stores and a loop-invariant Prop, with the step lemma proved in the block. The postcondition is the full reversal permutation.

examples.name: mutable
examples.title: Flow-sensitive mutable locals
examples.description: SSA versioning, conditional joins, let mutable, and for / while loops with [@vox.invariant], all with reflected arithmetic through the mutable reads.

examples.name: deadcode
examples.title: Dead code, proved dead
examples.description: A mutable local is written K 9, so matching L is impossible: the arm's facts are contradictory and unreachable_ discharges false from them. The K arm returns y with y = 9 by constructor injectivity.

examples.name: qsort
examples.title: In-place parallel quicksort
examples.description: The page's flagship: sorted-and-permutation on a borrowed slice, with a fork-join parallel psort under the same spec (borrow API and sort inlined for a single file). The heaviest example -- about 3s to verify, versus ~1s for the others. The inlined slice module is the trusted layer; every sort obligation past it is proved.

examples.name: counterexample
examples.title: When you're wrong (counterexample)
examples.description: A deliberately false spec: fib n = n + 1. Verification fails and the solver hands back a concrete witness -- n = 0, where fib 0 = 0, not 1. The one example here that does NOT verify.
